multilingual Wiktextract export. No individual article revision is supplied.

Modifications: retain attested 3–11-letter Romanian headwords in lexical POS
(excluding proper names), English glosses, usage labels and form/alternative
relationships with historical wordfreq spelling Zipf >=2.5. Omit media, examples,
quotations, etymology, translations, categories and other enrichment. Tiles use
NFC and uppercase. Ă, Â, Î, Ș and Ț remain distinct; all are single tiles.
Legacy Ş/Ţ are input and source-matching aliases of Ș/Ț, never of plain S/T.
No accent folding, transliteration, stress marks, hyphens or spaces are accepted.
Words requiring punctuation are excluded, not respelt by deleting punctuation.
Original source spelling is retained for attribution. Known misleading or inadequately qualified senses are explicitly removed.
Up to eight source
entries and eight senses per entry accompany each guess.
Broad guesses include attested inflections, alternatives and labelled uncommon,
historical, regional or sensitive senses. Answers require a standalone eligible
sense, Zipf >=4.3 and explicit independent model editorial approval.
Selection targets contemporary standard Romanian used in Romania, not exhaustive
regional separation. No native-human review or certification is claimed.

Frequency: wordfreq 3.0.2, Robyn Speer and contributors, revision
372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b, small_ro.msgpack.gz.
https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq/tree/372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b

Data: CC BY-SA 4.0. Software: MIT. Pinned README and MIT notice supplied.
Preserve all README source credits including OpenSubtitles and freely available
SUBTLEX, Marc Brysbaert and coauthors. No corpus sentences are redistributed.
For case-normalized/cedilla-alias spellings retain the maximum estimate, not a
sum. Historical mixed-corpus spelling frequency does not prove current
Romania-specific commonness or individual-sense frequency.
